config_name: MacBook Air 13-inch — M5 10-core CPU / 10-core GPU, 24GB RAM, 512GB SSD

specs.keyboard_notes: Magic Keyboard, Touch ID, Force Touch trackpad

battery.notes: Same 53.8Wh cell; extra RAM has negligible runtime impact.

reviews.quote: Apple's M5 SoC is the fastest single core processor you can buy.
The Apple MacBook Air 13 M5 has outstanding battery life.
The MacBook Air M5 is the sum of years of refinements, with a mix of premium design, strong performance, and solid battery life.

praises: 24GB unified memory handles heavy Xcode/Chrome-tab life and local LLMs that 16GB can't (r/macbook)
Still the cheapest way into 24GB + fast M5 in a 1.23 kg fanless chassis
Full workday battery regardless of RAM tier (RTINGS)
Silent — zero fan noise under any workload (NBC)
macOS ecosystem continuity with iPhone/iPad is the top reason buyers pick this over Windows ultrabooks (Amazon.ca reviews)
complaints: +C$300 for 24GB is expensive and non-upgradeable later (top r/macbook warning to buyers)
60Hz notched LCD at C$2,099 invites comparisons to cheaper OLED Windows machines
Fanless throttling on long exports/compiles despite the extra RAM
Two Thunderbolt ports only; dongles required for most desks
No Face ID — Touch ID only

design_philosophy: The RAM-forward tier: for buyers who run many apps, VMs, or on-device AI, 24GB in the silent Air chassis is the sweet spot Apple added this generation. Storage stays at the sensible 512GB baseline.
rating_notes: Ratings inferred from directly-tested M5 13-inch base (NBC 92%, RTINGS 8.3): +0.4 productivity / +0.7 ai_ml for 24GB vs 16GB, GPU tiers equal. Image is Apple specs-page CDN jpg. Sentiment from pro reviews + Amazon.ca aggregate; Reddit API blocked (403).
